name: Highland Park
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Highland Park, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas events in Highland Park, IL: the Port Clinton Square lighting, Breakfast with Santa, Winter Wonderland and Jingle Bell JAM at Ravinia.
lede: Highland Park opens the season with a Holiday Lighting in Port Clinton Square, where Santa and Hanukkah Harry arrive with a fire department escort. December brings park district Santa visits, a family concert at Ravinia and an ornament hunt on the trails at Heller Nature Center.
celebrates: The City of Highland Park starts the holidays downtown with its Holiday Lighting in Port Clinton Square. Families meet Santa and Hanukkah Harry, sing along with carolers, pose in a giant snow globe, write letters to the North Pole and share free popcorn and hot cocoa before Mayor Nancy Rotering lights the tree and menorah. The Park District of Highland Park fills December with Breakfast with Santa at Sunset Valley, Winter Wonderland at West Ridge Community Center, a luminary walk at Rosewood Beach and The Great Ornament Hunt at Heller Nature Center. Ravinia adds Jingle Bell JAM, a holiday sing-along concert it created especially for families.
lastyear: For 2025 the City billed its Holiday Lighting on Saturday, November 22, in Port Clinton Square as revamped, with an updated tree and menorah display. Santa and Hanukkah Harry arrived with a Highland Park Fire Department escort, Anna and Elsa from Frozen greeted kids, and the Highland Park High School Choir sang before Mayor Nancy Rotering waved a magic wand to turn on the lights. On Friday, December 5, 2025, Winter Wonderland at West Ridge Center brought Santa with real reindeer, a train ride through a holiday village, cookie decorating with Mrs. Claus and a new indoor ice rink.
facts: Ravinia, home of Jingle Bell JAM, began with a railroad. The Highland Park Historical Society says A.C. Frost bought the land in 1904 and opened an amusement park meant to draw riders to the Chicago and Milwaukee Electric Railroad. When the park struggled, a group of residents bought it, and it reopened in 1911 as a summer home for classical music. Ravinia says it will mark its 125th anniversary in 2029. At the city's Holiday Lighting, Santa and Hanukkah Harry greet families side by side, and the lights shine on both a tree and a menorah.
trains: Highland Park sits on Metra's Union Pacific North Line, which runs from Ogilvie Transportation Center in Chicago to Kenosha. Metra lists four city stops: Highland Park, Ravinia, Braeside and Ravinia Park, a summer stop at Ravinia's front gate. The Highland Park station is about a four minute walk from Port Clinton Square, and Braeside is a short walk from Bennett Gordon Hall for winter concerts. Ride north to Kenosha for vintage streetcars that stop at the Metra station, or head west to the Illinois Railway Museum in Union for the Happy Holiday Railway, a ride with Santa and his elves.
train_links: Ride the Happy Holiday Railway with Santa and his elves in Union, Illinois.
Vintage streetcars that stop at the Kenosha Metra station, at the end of the UP North Line.
traditions: Holiday Lighting in Port Clinton Square
The City lights its tree and menorah downtown in late November, with Santa, Hanukkah Harry, carolers, dancers and free popcorn and cocoa.
The park district fills West Ridge Community Center with Santa and Mrs. Claus, toy making with Buddy the Elf, carnival games and a Jolly Trolley ride with carolers.
Breakfast with Santa at Sunset Valley
Families share a buffet breakfast at The Clubhouse at Sunset Valley, with crafts, a visit from Santa and a small gift for each child.
Ravinia's indoor family concert in Bennett Gordon Hall mixes seasonal favorites, musical surprises and sing-alongs.
The Great Ornament Hunt at Heller
Heller Nature Center decorates its trees, and families hunt for ornaments hidden along the trails during trail hours.
At Rosewood Beach, families make nature ornaments, follow a luminary trail through the ravine and sip cocoa by a campfire.
kidfact: Ravinia started in 1904 as an amusement park built to get people riding the train. Today Metra trains still stop at Braeside, just a short walk from the park.
faq: Does Highland Park have a Christmas tree lighting?

Yes. The City holds its Holiday Lighting in Port Clinton Square, 600 Central Avenue, on a Saturday in late November. Santa and Hanukkah Harry arrive with a fire department escort, local dancers and the high school choir perform, and the mayor lights the tree and menorah. Families also find carolers, a giant snow globe for photos and free popcorn and hot cocoa.
Where can kids meet Santa in Highland Park?

Santa greets families at the Holiday Lighting in Port Clinton Square. The Park District of Highland Park also hosts Breakfast with Santa at The Clubhouse at Sunset Valley, with a buffet, crafts and a small gift, and Winter Wonderland at West Ridge Community Center, where kids visit Santa and Mrs. Claus and make toys with Buddy the Elf.
Do Highland Park holiday events include Hanukkah?

Yes. Hanukkah Harry joins Santa at the Holiday Lighting, and the City lights a menorah next to the tree in Port Clinton Square. At Winter Wonderland, kids can design their own dreidel, and in 2025 the park district added a Hanukkah Room.
Can we take Metra to Highland Park holiday events?

Yes. Metra's Union Pacific North Line stops at Highland Park, Ravinia and Braeside. The City says the Highland Park station is about a four minute walk from Port Clinton Square. For winter concerts at Ravinia, Braeside station is about a five minute walk from the South Entrance near Bennett Gordon Hall. Check Metra's schedule, since not every train stops at every station.
Are there free holiday activities in Highland Park?

The Great Ornament Hunt at Heller Nature Center is free and self guided, so families can stop by any time during trail hours. At the Holiday Lighting, the City hands out free popcorn and hot cocoa, and Santa gives out candy canes while supplies last. Most park district parties, like Winter Wonderland and Breakfast with Santa, need paid registration in advance.
Where should we park for the Holiday Lighting?

The City points to the parking garage under Port Clinton Square, nearby surface lots, a two level deck south of Central on First Street and St. Johns, and a large lot at 525 Central Avenue. You can also skip the car and take Metra to the Highland Park station or Pace Route 472 to the St. Johns and Central stop.
